verdict.rationale: Sill's own pairing model sets up trust in advance: each device pairs once, and after that only paired devices can connect. Remote Access via VPN or port forwarding lets you reach the Mac away from home, which implies later sessions need no one at the host. The docs never say outright that a reconnection needs no acceptance at the Mac, and there are no admin-managed credentials (no accounts, passwords or pre-provisioning), so this is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit confirmation that connections need no host-side acceptance, admin-configurable credentials or pre-provisioned pairing without someone at the host, independent hands-on corroboration of unattended use.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can set up unattended access to a machine with credentials configured in advance, so no one has to sit at the host to accept

citations.quote: Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
Sill's Settings › Devices on your Mac lists the devices you paired. Remove one you no longer use, or have lost.
